focus: Q4, the CI rebuild job, the seeder and the Gate 3 wording
noveltyJustification: Six findings are fully new (workflow guards, the sidecar staging gap, the missing postcondition, the token portability issue, the partial Gate 3 single-sourcing, the seeder triplication); one consolidates the loop-guard design and counts as half new.
ruledOut: Replacing the subject-based loop guard with an actor check
Treating the personal-token dependency as a defect

label: The rebuild workflow's core guards are sound: push-triggered to main and skilled/**, contents write, per-ref concurrency without cancel, a loop guard keyed to the rebuild commit subject (the token push runs under the owner's name), checkout with TRIGGER_INDEX_PUSH_TOKEN || github.token, and a push-failure message naming the secret and ruleset.

Hardening gap: the generator writes four outputs (index plus corpus-manifest.json, generation-diagnostics.json, phrase-variants.json) but the workflow stages only the index path, so sidecar drift from the same corpus change is never self-healed.

No postcondition and no retry: the job never runs generate-trigger-index.mjs --check after committing, and a push race fails as non-fast-forward with a ruleset-flavored error naming the wrong likely cause.

The token fallback couples CI healing to a personal credential: github.token cannot bypass the main ruleset, so the job only succeeds with the secret owned by a bypass actor; external users need the documented alternates (relax the ruleset for this path, or run the rebuild as a required bot check).

Gate 3 wording is only partially single-sourced: the four choice labels are exported constants and the Pi dialog consumes all four, but the question and notice menus still inline option C and use two different D wordings, and GATE_3_CHOICE_RELATED is unused by either list; the series-parent copy surface is 34 files outside specs.

The seeder duplicates the template-default phrases a third time: create.sh hardcodes five four-phrase arrays restating the templates and the phrase-judge frozen sets, plus a stop-word list shared with the cleanup tool and pinned by a test; pinning catches disagreement but the runtime still holds three copies.

The loop guard is message-shaped rather than identity-shaped: a merge whose head commit subject starts with the rebuild message is skipped, and workflow_dispatch bypasses the guard by design; acceptable today, fragile if the commit message ever changes.

direction: Replacing the subject-based loop guard with an actor check
reason: The token push runs under the owner's name, which is exactly why the original actor check failed.

direction: Treating the personal-token dependency as a defect
reason: In this repository it is the only mechanism satisfying the ruleset; the hardening is documenting alternates.
